{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-la-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"cd763aa18036f9e0cc087880eb10998afddf4d526b42dd03889c24c87bbe79d4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-la-class-std:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"8fb2294cb50570a3a0fabb25acba3418dba999eb7dd305cc58b73fdf38975613","source_liveness_sha256":"1105a92b5841d065519de4b7fbea05111880de6d2bb8804066a972d19c63b5a0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Flag persons, signals, markings and roundabouts","heading":"Flag persons, signals, markings and roundabouts","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"# Flag persons, signals, markings and roundabouts

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
White lane markings divide streams of traffic moving in the same direction; vehicles should remain between them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
A single solid white line warns that a lane change is hazardous and should be crossed only with great care. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
A wider solid white line represents a greater lane-change hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
A dashed white lane line may be crossed when the maneuver is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A01
A white edge line marks the roadway’s right edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A01
On divided roads, a yellow edge line may mark the left edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A01
Crossing double solid white lines separating same-direction lanes is prohibited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A01
Red raised pavement markers or reflectors warn that the vehicle is facing against traffic and must not enter that roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A01
Advance railroad pavement markings use a large white X and two white R letters. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A01
At the described railroad approach, a solid yellow centerline prevents passing and a white transverse line marks the stopping location. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A01
The guide directs vehicles to use the right lane unless passing, preparing to turn left or responding to congestion in the right lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A01
The guide says a vehicle in a left lane must not move more slowly than traffic to its right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A01
A vehicle moving below the normal traffic speed belongs in the right lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A02
A shared center left-turn lane is outlined with both solid and broken yellow markings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A02
Traffic from either direction may use the shared center lane for a left turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A02
A two-way center left-turn lane may not be used to pass or to continue traveling along the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A02
A solid white stop line across the lane identifies where a required stop should be made. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A02
Crosswalks commonly have two white transverse lines; some add diagonal or lengthwise stripes for visibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A02
Drivers must stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian crosswalk may be located between intersections and may have a crossing sign. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A02
White words or arrows painted in a lane tell the driver which direction that lane permits. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A02
When a lane arrow permits several directions, the driver may select one of those indicated directions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A03
If already in a required-turn lane when wanting to go straight, complete the turn and return by going around the block. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A03
Stopping in a required-turn lane while waiting to change lanes blocks traffic; other drivers do not expect a sudden stop or lane change. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A03
A roundabout is a circular junction in which entering traffic yields to traffic already circulating. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A03
The guide describes a roundabout speed of fifteen miles per hour or less as adequate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A03
Yield to vehicles approaching from the left before entering a roundabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A03
The guide directs drivers to keep moving once inside the roundabout because circulating vehicles have priority. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A03
Use destination signs to select the roundabout exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A03
Before leaving a roundabout, look right, check the mirror and signal the exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
